CREATING DAY_NAME, MONTH_NAME & PROFIT_MARGIN

In [20]:
cursor = conn.cursor()
cursor.execute("""
ALTER TABLE global_ecommerce_sales
ADD DAY_NAME VARCHAR(20),
MONTH_NAME VARCHAR(20),
PROFIT_MARGIN DECIMAL(20, 2)


""")
conn.commit()
In [21]:
cursor.execute("""
UPDATE global_ecommerce_sales
SET
    DAY_NAME = DATENAME(WEEKDAY, Order_Date),
    MONTH_NAME = DATENAME(MONTH, Order_Date),
    PROFIT_MARGIN = (Profit / NULLIF(Total_Sales, 0)) * 100
""")

conn.commit()

SALES_BEFORE_DISCOUNT | SALES_AFTER_DISCOUNT | DISCOUNT_GIVEN | TOTAL_PROFIT | PROFIT_MARGIN | GROSS_LOSS | TOTAL_ORDERS | TOTAL_CUSTOMERS

In [23]:
pd.read_sql("""
SELECT SUM(Quantity * Unit_Price) AS SALES_BEFORE_DISCOUNT,
SUM(Total_Sales) AS SALES_AFTER_DISCOUNT,
SUM(Quantity * Unit_Price) - SUM(Total_Sales) AS DISCOUNT_GIVEN,
SUM(Profit) AS TOTAL_PROFIT,
ROUND(SUM(Profit) * 100.0 / SUM(Total_Sales), 2) AS PROFIT_MARGIN,
SUM(CASE WHEN Profit < 0 THEN Profit ELSE 0 END) AS GROSS_LOSS,
COUNT(DISTINCT Order_ID)      AS TOTAL_ORDERS,
COUNT(DISTINCT Customer_Name) AS TOTAL_CUSTOMERS
FROM global_ecommerce_sales;

""",engine)

GROWTH OR DECLINE BY MONTH & YEAR

In [28]:
pd.read_sql("""
WITH MONTHLY_SALES AS (SELECT YEAR(Order_Date) AS YEAR, MONTH(Order_Date) AS MONTH, MONTH_NAME,
SUM(Total_Sales) AS TOTAL_SALES
FROM global_ecommerce_sales
GROUP BY YEAR(Order_Date), MONTH(Order_Date), MONTH_NAME),
WITH_PREV AS (SELECT*,
LAG(Total_Sales) OVER(ORDER BY YEAR, MONTH) AS PREVIOUS_MONTH_SALES FROM MONTHLY_SALES)
SELECT YEAR, MONTH, MONTH_NAME, TOTAL_SALES, PREVIOUS_MONTH_SALES,
TOTAL_SALES - PREVIOUS_MONTH_SALES AS GROWTH_SALES,
ROUND((TOTAL_SALES - PREVIOUS_MONTH_SALES)*100./NULLIF(PREVIOUS_MONTH_SALES, 0), 2) AS GROWTH_PERCENTAGE,
CASE  WHEN TOTAL_SALES > PREVIOUS_MONTH_SALES THEN 'Growth'
WHEN TOTAL_SALES < PREVIOUS_MONTH_SALES THEN 'Decline'
ELSE 'No Change' END PERFORMANCE
FROM WITH_PREV
ORDER BY YEAR, MONTH;



""",engine)

Conclusion¶

The analysis shows that the e-commerce business is performing profitably, generating 484,559.34 in sales, 158,872.32 in profit, and a 32.79% overall profit margin across 2,000 orders and 1,534 customers. Consumer customers are the strongest segment, contributing the highest sales, profit, quantity, and profit margin. Furniture is the largest revenue-generating product category, while Clothing & Accessories delivers the highest profit margin.

The analysis also identifies several areas requiring management attention. Profitability decreases consistently as discount levels increase, with profit margin falling from 38.72% at no discount to 13.42% at a 30% discount. Office Supplies has the weakest category margin at 17.12%, while two products—Paper Clips Box 500pc and Highlighters Neon Pack 6—generate negative profit. Geographically, Europe generates the highest regional sales, while North America achieves the strongest regional profit margin. The monthly analysis also shows considerable fluctuations in performance, including periods of significant growth and decline.

Overall, the business has a healthy profit position, but profitability can potentially be improved through better discount control, optimization of low-margin products and categories, and closer monitoring of underperforming regions and products.

Recommendations¶

  1. Control high discounts Review discount strategies above 10–15%, as higher discount levels are associated with substantially lower profit margins. Discounts should be targeted toward products or customer segments where they can generate additional demand without significantly reducing profitability.

  2. Review Office Supplies profitability Office Supplies has the lowest category margin at 17.12%. Management should investigate supplier costs, pricing, discount levels, and shipping costs to identify opportunities for margin improvement.

  3. Investigate loss-making products Review Paper Clips Box 500pc and Highlighters Neon Pack 6 at the transaction level. Check purchase cost, selling price, discounts, and shipping expenses before deciding whether to reprice, discontinue, or bundle these products.

  4. Protect and expand the Consumer segment Consumer customers generate the highest sales and profit and also have the strongest segment margin. Marketing and retention strategies should focus on increasing repeat purchases and customer lifetime value within this segment.

  5. Use high-margin products strategically Clothing & Accessories has the highest category margin at 37.64%. The business should consider promoting high-margin products and using them in bundles with lower-margin products.

  6. Improve Furniture profitability Furniture generates the highest sales and profit but has a lower margin than Clothing & Accessories. The company should investigate product-level margins, sourcing costs, discounts, and shipping expenses within Furniture.

  7. Investigate regional profitability Middle East & Africa has the lowest regional margin at 30.82%. Further analysis should examine product mix, discounts, shipping costs, and customer segments within the region before making strategic changes.

  8. Use monthly performance monitoring Continue monitoring month-over-month sales growth using LAG() and establish alerts for unusually large declines. This can help management react earlier to changes in demand.

  9. Optimize shipping costs Analyze shipping cost by region, product category, and order value to identify areas where logistics expenses are reducing profitability.

  10. Build a recurring management dashboard The final analysis could be converted into a Power BI dashboard showing sales, profit, margin, customer segments, regional performance, product performance, discount impact, and monthly growth so that these metrics can be monitored continuously.
